title: Bandi Chhor Divas 2026: Diwali at the Golden Temple Amritsar
summary: What Bandi Chhor Divas at the Golden Temple looks like in 2026. The 48-hour celebration, fireworks over the Sarovar, Langar and a practical travel plan.
body_markdown:
The celebration at the Golden Temple on Diwali night is not Diwali in the Hindu sense. It is Bandi Chhor Divas, a Sikh observance that marks the liberation of Guru Hargobind, the sixth Sikh Guru, from imprisonment at Gwalior Fort during the Mughal period.


The historical account is specific. Guru Hargobind was imprisoned alongside 52 Hindu princes. When the Mughal emperor offered his release, the Guru refused to leave unless all 52 princes were freed with him. The emperor agreed, but on the condition that only those who could hold onto his cloak would walk out. Guru Hargobind had a cloak made with 52 tassels, one for each prince, and led all of them out.


That story is why the Golden Temple is illuminated on this date. The celebration is about a specific act of liberation, not the broader Diwali narrative, and the scale of the illumination at the[Harmandir Sahib](https://www.goldentempleamritsar.org/) reflects that significance.


## **What Happens During the 48-Hour Celebration**


Bandi Chhor Divas 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. The celebration runs continuously for approximately 48 hours, starting from the evening of November 7 through the morning of November 9.


### **Two Days Before: Akhand Path Begins**


The Akhand Path, a continuous unbroken reading of the[Guru Granth Sahib](https://www.srigranth.org/servlet/gurbani.gurbani?S=y) , begins two days before the celebration. The reading runs for 48 hours straight, with relay readers ensuring the recitation does not pause. The path concludes on the morning of November 8.


### **The Evening: Illumination and Fireworks**


The primary spectacle is the evening of November 8, though the illumination begins on November 7 evening as well.


What you see:


- The entire Golden Temple complex lit with thousands of decorative lights
- The Sarovar (sacred pool) reflecting the illuminated Harmandir Sahib
- A fireworks display over the Sarovar lasting approximately 30 to 45 minutes
- The parikrama (walkway around the pool) packed with devotees and visitors


The best viewing positions for the fireworks are from the Dukh Bhanjani Beri side (northern edge of the parikrama) and from the entrance bridge facing the Harmandir Sahib directly.


### **Through the Night: Open Darshan**


The temple stays open through the night. This is where the experience diverges from what most visitors expect.


The 2:00 to 5:00 AM window is the most atmospheric period of the entire celebration. The crowds thin. The continuous kirtan fills the sanctum. The lit temple against the dark sky, reflected in the Sarovar with no daytime haze, is the version of the Golden Temple that the daytime visitor never sees.


If you can stay awake past midnight, this is the experience that justifies the trip.


### **Morning: Asa Di Var**


The morning kirtan, Asa Di Var, is performed at approximately 4:00 to 5:00 AM. This happens daily at the Golden Temple, but on Bandi Chhor Divas it carries additional significance. The pre-dawn singing in the lit sanctum is considered one of the spiritual highlights of the Sikh calendar.


## **The Langar**


The Golden Temple’s Langar (community kitchen) is the largest free kitchen in the world. It serves meals to all visitors regardless of faith, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. On Bandi Chhor Divas, the Langar serves an estimated 100,000+ meals.


The experience of sitting on the floor in the Langar hall, receiving chapati and dal alongside thousands of others from every background, is itself a reason to visit. The Langar operates continuously during the 48-hour celebration.


The[Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC)](https://www.sgpc.net/) manages both the Golden Temple and the Langar operations.


## **What Else to Do in Amritsar**


A Bandi Chhor Divas trip to Amritsar gives 2 to 3 days of content beyond the temple celebration.


### **Jallianwala Bagh**


The memorial site of the[1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre](https://jallianwalabagh.org/about/) is a 5-minute walk from the Golden Temple. The bullet marks on the walls and the narrow passage through which troops entered are preserved. A sound and light show runs in the evenings.


### **Wagah Border Ceremony**


The daily flag-lowering ceremony at the Wagah-Attari border crossing is about 28 km from the city centre. The ceremony takes place at sunset, runs roughly 45 minutes, and draws a larger crowd than usual during the Diwali weekend. Allow 45 minutes for the drive from the Golden Temple.


### **Partition Museum**


The[Partition Museum](https://www.partitionmuseum.org/) at Town Hall in the old city is one of the few museums in the world dedicated to the 1947 partition. Personal artefacts, letters and testimonies form the core collection.


### **Heritage Walk and Food**


The lanes behind the Golden Temple carry the old Amritsar character: narrow streets, traditional havelis, Guru Ka Mahal (Guru Ram Das’s residence) and the silverware shops of Guru Bazaar.


Amritsar’s food identity is distinct. Kulcha at Bharawan Da Dhaba, lassi at Ahuja Lassi, and the Dhabba Wali Gali near the Golden Temple carry their own pilgrim food tradition.


## **How to Reach Amritsar**


**By Bus from Delhi:** Overnight journey, roughly 8 to 9 hours. Book at least 2 to 3 weeks ahead as the Delhi-Amritsar corridor sees heavy demand during Diwali and Gurpurab.


**By Train:** Amritsar Junction is connected to Delhi by the Shatabdi Express (roughly 6 hours) and multiple overnight trains. The station is about 2 km from the Golden Temple.


**By Air:**[Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport](https://www.aai.aero/en/airports/amritsar) is about 11 km from the city centre.


## **Where to Stay**


Hotels near the Golden Temple fill early for Bandi Chhor Divas. The temple’s own Niwas (guesthouse) offers basic pilgrim accommodation, but availability during the festival is extremely limited.


Hotels along Lawrence Road, Queens Road and near the railway station carry a wider inventory. Book at least 3 weeks before November 8 for the Diwali weekend.


## **November Weather in Amritsar**


November temperatures range between 10 and 25 degrees Celsius. Evenings and early mornings are cool. If you plan to stay through the overnight darshan window (2 to 5 AM), carry a warm jacket.


## **Combining with Gurpurab**


Guru Nanak Jayanti falls on November 24, just 16 days after Bandi Chhor Divas. The Golden Temple hosts another major celebration on that date. Travellers who can make a second trip or extend their stay have the rare opportunity to experience two of the Sikh calendar’s most significant days at the same gurudwara within a single month.


***Note:*** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **When is bandi chhor divas 2026 golden temple?**


Bandi Chhor Divas falls on Sunday, November 8, coinciding with Diwali. The celebration runs approximately 48 hours.


### **What is the difference between Diwali and Bandi Chhor Divas?**


Diwali celebrates the return of Lord Ram. Bandi Chhor Divas marks Guru Hargobind’s liberation of 52 princes from Gwalior Fort.


### **What time are the fireworks at the Golden Temple?**


The fireworks over the Sarovar begin after dark on November 8 evening and run for roughly 30 to 45 minutes.


### **Is the Golden Temple open all night during Bandi Chhor Divas?**


The temple stays open through the night. The 2 to 5 AM window is the quietest and most atmospheric.


### **How many meals does the Golden Temple Langar serve?**


The Langar serves an estimated 100,000+ meals on Bandi Chhor Divas, free to all visitors regardless of faith.


### **How do I reach Amritsar from Delhi?**


Overnight bus (8 to 9 hours), Shatabdi Express (6 hours), or flights to Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport (11 km from the city).


### **Where is the best spot to watch the fireworks?**


The Dukh Bhanjani Beri side of the parikrama and the entrance bridge facing the Harmandir Sahib give the best views.


### **How early should I book hotels?**


Book at least 3 weeks before November 8. Hotels near the Golden Temple fill first.


### **What should I wear to the Golden Temple?**


Cover your head (scarves are available at the entrance). Remove shoes before entering. Modest clothing covering shoulders and legs.


### **Can I combine Bandi Chhor Divas with Guru Nanak Jayanti?**


Guru Nanak Jayanti is November 24, 16 days after Bandi Chhor Divas. Both happen at the Golden Temple with distinct celebrations.
